viewer_question: Why do shallow grooves beside a lane make a car rumble?
hypothesis: A viewer-first opening and an explicit visual payoff may improve comprehension and interest; no growth or view-count outcome is assumed.

facts: Rumble strips alert drivers through sound and vibration when a vehicle leaves the travel lane.
The illustrated shoulder configuration uses milled cuts; rumble strips can also be raised or placed elsewhere.
scope_limits: Do not generalize the shown geometry to all rumble strips.
Do not claim that rumble strips steer a car, guarantee recovery or prevent every crash.
Kinematic motion and illustrative sound are explanatory, not calibrated tire/vehicle dynamics or a real recording.

controls.voice: same existing approved English voice across all variants; no provider/model change
controls.speech_rate: same natural rate; measure actual speech before locking duration; no forced speed-up
controls.neutral_title: Why the road makes your car rumble
controls.music_and_sfx: same approved tracks, illustrative rumble and mix for equivalent events
controls.fact_payload: same four roles: groove location, repeated tire contact, audible/tactile warning, driver response
controls.packaging: same neutral title/cover in the initial offline comparison

required_next_evidence: Verify source scene, dependencies and reusable license on the render host.
Inspect real opening motion for each variant, including smooth/grooved contact and lane context.
Verify contact, geometry, no clipping and meaningful changes before full renders.
Full videos must cover their actual 900 output frames; a 15-frame proof is insufficient.

beats.narration_en: Those grooves beside the lane are rumble strips.
beats.visual_evidence_required: Lane-edge overview establishes the car, white edge line and grooved shoulder immediately.

beats.narration_en: They warn drivers with sound and vibration when a vehicle drifts out of its lane.
beats.visual_evidence_required: Two real events within five seconds: tire enters the grooved band, then a section view exposes the cuts.

beats.narration_en: On this road, the strips are cut into the asphalt.
beats.visual_evidence_required: Fixed-camera section of actual milled geometry, visibly below the smooth adjoining lane.

beats.narration_en: As the tire crosses the cuts, repeated contact makes the car rumble.
beats.visual_evidence_required: Continuous native wheel motion across successive grooves; matching illustrative rumble and vibration.

beats.narration_en: The warning gives the driver a chance to notice the drift.
beats.visual_evidence_required: Return to the same road context with car approaching the edge; no invented crash.

beats.narration_en: The grooves give the warning. The driver makes the correction.
beats.visual_evidence_required: Clearly attributed driver-initiated correction; retain a final spatial answer showing lane and shoulder.

beats.narration_en: The road looks almost flat. So why does this tire rumble?
beats.visual_evidence_required: Show smooth-lane contact then actual grooved-shoulder contact, with the same wheel and scene scale. These are separate fixed-camera shots; no hidden geometry or fake depth.

beats.narration_en: Look beside the white line: shallow grooves are cut into the asphalt.
beats.visual_evidence_required: A native section reveal exposes the true recessed surface and locates it beside the edge line.

beats.narration_en: The tire repeatedly crosses them, creating sound and vibration.
beats.visual_evidence_required: Continuous contact close-up; the tire and groove must remain visible together.

beats.narration_en: That disturbance is deliberate: it warns a driver drifting out of the lane.
beats.visual_evidence_required: Wider location reveal connects the surprising rumble to the car reaching the shoulder.

beats.narration_en: The warning gives the driver a chance to notice the drift.
beats.visual_evidence_required: Visible cause and response; avoid implying that every warned driver reacts in time.

beats.narration_en: The driver still has to notice the warning and correct the car's path.
beats.visual_evidence_required: Same driver-response footage pool as A; resolve why the shallow-looking surface produced the warning.

beats.narration_en: Your tire reaches the shoulder. Suddenly, the car starts to rumble.
beats.visual_evidence_required: First frame identifies a car, its tire and lane edge. Within three seconds the tire reaches actual grooves and the warning begins.

beats.narration_en: What is the road trying to tell you?
beats.visual_evidence_required: Maintain spatial continuity; reveal the recessed grooves as the candidate answer, without unrelated suspense shots.

beats.narration_en: These shallow grooves make repeated contact with the tire.
beats.visual_evidence_required: Native fixed-camera contact view follows the same tire across successive grooves.

beats.narration_en: That creates sound and vibration you can notice inside the car.
beats.visual_evidence_required: Wheel/contact detail and nearby body response explain the audible/tactile cue; disclose stylized kinematic motion.

beats.narration_en: It is a warning that your vehicle is drifting out of the lane.
beats.visual_evidence_required: Wider road context answers what the signal means, with the edge line and car present together.

beats.narration_en: The driver needs to respond and guide the car back. That is what the rumble is for.
beats.visual_evidence_required: Show driver-initiated correction and the original lane/shoulder relationship. End the question asked at the start.

review.independent_initial_comprehension: First viewing only; ask an unfamiliar English-speaking viewer to describe the situation after 3 seconds. Prior exposure to another variant invalidates a naive first-view result.

criteria.question: Can a new viewer identify the tire, road edge, and immediate situation within three seconds?
criteria.evidence_required: Actual 0–3s playback, reviewer answer, and timestamps; script text alone is insufficient.

criteria.question: Does a visible change create a clear question in the opening?
criteria.evidence_required: Actual smooth/grooved contact or equivalent physical change; a question caption by itself is insufficient.

criteria.question: Does the middle introduce an explanatory fact or physical change?
criteria.evidence_required: Timestamped geometry/contact/response change, with what the viewer learns.

criteria.question: Does the ending answer the opening's specific question?
criteria.evidence_required: Opening/payoff paired timestamps and a concise statement of the answer.

criteria.question: Does the 3D show the causal mechanism?
criteria.evidence_required: Continuous contact and response footage; car movement alone is insufficient.

review.technical_and_editorial: Both must pass; planning scores never override technical QA or evidence bindings.
review.sampling: Use each actual beat and transition, including changed mechanism intervals. Review the first three seconds and critical motion as clips; fixed global timestamps alone are insufficient.
